method: Housekeeping and the recurring pain of app work, catalogued once so the factory starts from them and the AI designs only what is different. Each part says what it gives and what goes wrong without it. The universal ones are in the team minimum; the rest are called for by what the schematic says.

parts.name: Lists: paging, sorting and filters
parts.gives: Every list pages, sorts and filters on the server with a stable order and an opaque cursor; each person's last sort and filters are kept
parts.without: Lists that load everything, reorder on refresh, or lose the filter on the way back

parts.name: Edit conflicts
parts.gives: Every record carries a version; saving a stale copy is stopped, fields that do not clash merge, and the person sees exactly what clashed
parts.without: Last write silently wins, and a colleague's change disappears

parts.name: Trash and restore
parts.gives: Delete moves a record and everything that depends on it to a trash with a retention window; restore puts all of it back; purging is a separate, recorded act
parts.without: Deleted by mistake with no way back, or deletions that leave broken references

parts.name: Reference data
parts.gives: Code lists (categories, terms, states, reasons) as versioned data with effective dates, edited in admin with a preview, never written into the code
parts.without: Adding one option to a list needs a release

studentAdvocate.from: refdata: effective dates, replacements, safe versions

parts.name: Data retention sweeper
parts.gives: Each record kind's retention period, from the data sheets, enforced by a nightly job that archives or purges and records what it did and why
parts.without: Data kept forever by default, and a compliance finding

parts.name: Backfills
parts.gives: A change that must fill existing records runs as a resumable, checkpointed job with a dry run, progress, and a count that must reconcile before it is done
parts.without: A migration that times out halfway and leaves records in two shapes

studentAdvocate.from: jobs: checkpointed backfills with a dry run

parts.name: Backup restore drills
parts.gives: Backups restored to a scratch environment on a schedule and checked against record counts and every integrity rule
parts.without: Backups nobody ever restored, found unusable on the worst day

parts.name: Money and rounding
parts.gives: Amounts held as whole minor units with their currency, one rounding rule per currency, and splits that always add back to the total
parts.without: Floating-point cents, totals off by a penny, and rounding that differs by screen

parts.name: Names, addresses and phone numbers
parts.gives: Names as people give them (preferred and legal, any script, any length), and addresses and phone numbers validated and formatted to international standards
parts.without: Forms that reject real names, mangle addresses and refuse numbers from abroad

parts.name: Timeouts, retries and circuit breakers
parts.gives: Every outward call has a timeout, a bounded number of retries with backoff and jitter, and a breaker that fails fast while a service is down and recovers on its own
parts.without: One slow service hangs every request, and retries pile on until it falls over

parts.name: Idempotent requests
parts.gives: Every create and every outward action carries an idempotency key; a repeat returns the first result, and the same key with different content is refused
parts.without: Double clicks and retries make two payments, two records and two emails

parts.name: Dead letters and replay
parts.gives: A job that keeps failing goes to a dead-letter queue with its last error; after a fix an admin replays it, once, and the replay is recorded
parts.without: Failed jobs vanish, or retry forever

parts.name: Cron watchdog
parts.gives: Every scheduled job checks in; a missed, overlong or overlapping run alerts, and a lease stops two copies running at once
parts.without: The nightly job stopped three weeks ago and nobody knew

parts.name: Long tasks with progress
parts.gives: Anything longer than a few seconds runs as a job with progress, cancel and a notice when it is done, surviving a refresh
parts.without: Spinners that time out, and work lost when the page reloads

parts.name: Graceful shutdown
parts.gives: On a deploy or scale-in the service stops taking work, finishes what is in flight within a deadline, then exits
parts.without: Requests cut off mid-write on every deploy

studentAdvocate.from: health: drain with a grace period

parts.name: Bounces and unsubscribes
parts.gives: Bounce, complaint and unsubscribe handling with suppression lists, one-click unsubscribe, and signed sending domains
parts.without: Messages to dead addresses, mail in spam folders, and messages to people who asked to stop

parts.name: Notification preferences and digests
parts.gives: Each person chooses channel, frequency and quiet hours for each kind of message; low-urgency messages batch into a digest
parts.without: So many messages that people turn all of them off

parts.name: API versioning and deprecation
parts.gives: Versioned routes, deprecation and sunset headers with dates, and use of old versions reported before anything is removed
parts.without: A client broken without warning

parts.name: Upload safety
parts.gives: Uploads checked for type, size and malware before use, stored outside the web root and served with safe headers
parts.without: A file upload as a way in

parts.name: Account lifecycle
parts.gives: Invite, activate, deactivate, reactivate and offboard, with every grant removed on the way out; inactive accounts flagged and disabled after a set time
parts.without: Accounts of people long gone, still working

parts.name: Session expiry warning
parts.gives: A warning before a session ends with a way to stay signed in; work in progress kept if it does end
parts.without: A long form lost to a silent timeout

studentAdvocate.from: sessions: warning before idle or absolute expiry

parts.name: Secret rotation
parts.gives: Every secret has an owner and a rotation date; rotation runs without downtime, and a secret past its date alerts
parts.without: Keys from years ago that nobody dares rotate

studentAdvocate.from: config and crypto: rotation dates, overdue alerts, and a key ring that rotates without downtime

parts.name: Break-glass access
parts.gives: Emergency access that is time-boxed, needs a written reason, alerts on use, and is reviewed afterwards
parts.without: Shared admin passwords kept for emergencies

studentAdvocate.from: accounts: break-glass with a reason, time box and review list

parts.name: Terms and consent versions
parts.gives: Which version of the terms and of each consent each person accepted, and when; they are asked again, plainly, when it changes
parts.without: Not knowing what someone agreed to, or when

parts.name: Dependency upkeep
parts.gives: Dependencies updated on a schedule by the factory, security advisories first, each update through every check before it merges
parts.without: Two years of upgrades at once, under pressure

parts.name: Expiry watch
parts.gives: Certificates, domains, keys, tokens, contracts and security contacts with their expiry dates, alerting well before each one
parts.without: The certificate expired on a Saturday

parts.name: Cost meter and budgets
parts.gives: Spend per service and per feature, against budgets, with an alert before each ceiling and a hard stop where one is set
parts.without: A surprise bill

parts.name: Configuration drift check
parts.gives: Each environment's live configuration compared with what was declared and signed; drift alerts and is shown in the admin console
parts.without: Works in test, fails in production, and nobody can say why

studentAdvocate.from: config: drift against the signed declaration

parts.name: Status page
parts.gives: The status of each part of the service, incidents and their updates, fed by the service-level alerts rather than typed by hand
parts.without: Support flooded during an outage, and people guessing

studentAdvocate.from: health: the status model from checks and incidents

parts.name: Incidents and postmortems
parts.gives: Every alert links its runbook; every incident gets a timeline, a cause, and a defect, a test and a ratchet so it cannot happen the same way again
parts.without: The same outage, again

parts.name: Load and soak checks
parts.gives: The load the schematic expects run against each release candidate for long enough to find leaks, with the latency budget as the gate
parts.without: Fine with ten people, down with a thousand

parts.name: Security scanning
parts.gives: Static analysis, dependency, container and secret scanning on every change, and a dynamic scan of each release candidate
parts.without: Known holes shipped

parts.name: Log retention and redaction
parts.gives: Logs kept for as long as policy says, sensitive fields redacted where they are written, and every line findable by its request
parts.without: Personal data in logs, kept forever

studentAdvocate.from: observe: redaction where written and retention rules

parts.name: Housekeeping console
parts.gives: One admin page listing every housekeeping job (sweeps, drills, rotations, expiries, watchdogs, upkeep), when each last ran, what it did, and what is due
parts.without: Housekeeping that silently stopped

parts.name: Friendly error pages
parts.gives: Not found, not allowed, something broke, and offline pages that say what happened and what to do next, with a reference to quote
parts.without: Raw errors, or a blank page

parts.name: Loading, empty and error states
parts.gives: Every view designed for loading, empty, partly loaded and failed, so nothing is ever a blank screen or a spinner forever
parts.without: Blank screens, and spinners that never stop

parts.name: First run
parts.gives: A first-run path that gets a new person to their first success, skippable, and never shown again once done
parts.without: People who never find the one thing they came for

parts.name: Maintenance mode and notices
parts.gives: A planned-work banner ahead of time, read-only mode during maintenance, and a clear page while down
parts.without: People caught mid-task by a planned outage

studentAdvocate.from: health: windows, notice and read-only rule

parts.name: Print and save as PDF
parts.gives: Every record and report prints cleanly and saves as an accessible PDF
parts.without: Screenshots as the only way to keep a copy

parts.name: What's new
parts.gives: Release notes in plain words, written from the change notice and shown once to the people each change affects
parts.without: Changes that surprise the people who rely on them

parts.name: Public pages: metadata and sitemap
parts.gives: Titles, descriptions, social cards, a sitemap and robots rules for every public page
parts.without: Invisible to search, and ugly when shared

parts.name: Leaving with your data
parts.gives: Everything an organisation keeps, exported on request in open formats with the schema and a data dictionary
parts.without: Locked in, with no way out

parts.name: Folders and paths
parts.gives: Nested folders with stable ids, where a change re-tags the item and every folder above it and keeps folder sizes, so anything that syncs or caches skips what did not change
parts.without: Paths stored in every row, renames that rewrite thousands of records, and sync that rescans everything to find one change

parts.name: Locks and leases
parts.gives: An exclusive hold with an owner and a time limit that ends on its own, so two people never save over each other and a crashed holder never locks anyone out
parts.without: Lock rows nobody clears, files locked until an admin edits the database, and edits lost to whoever saved last
